intelligence.human_view: Think of it like the front door of a house: one door, clearly labelled, and behind it a hallway with every room's door in plain view. Not three doors with clever names — one door that says what it is, and a hallway where you pick the room you want. The legal pages are rooms that already exist; they just need to be furnished like the rest of the house.
intelligence.simple_view: One button! Just one! And it says "Agreement"! Tap it and you see a list of ALL the law pages — the oath, the laws, the rules — and you can scroll and pick the one you want! And every law page looks just like the other pages, with three boards!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — one button, dear, just one, and it says "Agreement"! Tap it and there's a lovely list of all the law pages, love — the oath, the laws, the rules — and you scroll and pick the one you want, dear! And every law page is filled out proper, just like the other pages, in three boards!
intelligence.naya_view: A footer that asks "What is this?" makes the visitor do the work of figuring out what the button is. A button that says "Agreement" tells them before they tap. That is the whole ruling in one line: the label is the promise, and the promise is the agreement. Behind it, the table of contents does the same job for the legal pages — every page that was there before, in one scrollable list, each page filled out and built like the other pages, three boards each — so the law reads like the rest of the system instead of a forgotten annex. And the sequencing is part of the ruling: one lane, one round at a time, so the footer round waits for the bigger-text round to finish on the same two pages, comes back staged, and never goes live without his tap.
